guidance: Quantities only. The one gallon per person per day rate covers drinking and sanitation for a normally active household; hot weather, hard physical work, pregnancy, illness, nursing and pets raise the real need and are not modelled. No treatment, container or medical advice is given.
method: The requirement is headcount x days x one US gallon per person per day, the Ready.gov baseline for drinking and sanitation. The same volume is converted to liters at 3.785411784 L per gallon, three quarters of a gallon per person per day is reported as the drinking share and the remainder as sanitation and cooking, stored gallons divided by the daily rate give the days covered, and the difference from the requirement is reported as a shortfall or a surplus. Each container plan divides the requirement by the container volume (5 gal jug, 1 gal bottle, 0.5 L bottle, 12 L case of 24) and rounds up to whole containers, so the capacity column exceeds the requirement except where it divides exactly. The replacement date is today plus six calendar months, clamped to the last day of the month, for water that is not commercially bottled. Inputs are a whole headcount from 1 to 12, a whole day count from 1 to 30 and a stored volume from 0 to 2000 gallons; everything runs in the browser with no uploads, storage or network calls.
